source: Canadian National Autism Foundation, cnaf.net/provinceres.html; each entry checked on its own website

entries.name: Goldwater Droit
entries.description: A Montreal family law litigation firm that handles divorce and separation, custody and parenting disputes, child and spousal support, youth protection (DPJ) cases, and estate and succession disputes, including capacity challenges. In youth protection matters it represents parents, children and extended family.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention fees.
entries.address: 3500 Boulevard de Maisonneuve Ouest, #2310 Westmount, Quebec H3Z 3C1
entries.evidence: Goldwater Droit is a Montreal family law litigation firm.
entries.notes: CNAF links to goldwaterdube.com ('Goldwater, Dube Firm'); that domain now redirects to goldwaterdroit.com, where CNAF's two pages return 404, so the firm's current services page is used. CNAF lists it on its national page, but it is a Quebec family law firm (office in Westmount); the site does not mention autism or disability services.

entries.name: Goldwater Droit
entries.description: Family law firm with its office in Westmount (Montreal) whose lawyers represent clients across Quebec in divorce and separation, parenting and custody disputes, child and spousal support, youth protection (DPJ) cases and estate disputes. People book a consultation with one of its lawyers.
entries.cost_note: Private law firm; the site suggests asking about the hourly rate and scope of work when choosing a lawyer.
entries.address: 3500 Boulevard de Maisonneuve Ouest, #2310 Westmount, Quebec H3Z 3C1
entries.evidence: Our Montreal family lawyers advise and represent clients across Quebec in divorce, parenting, support, and property disputes.
entries.notes: CNAF links to goldwaterdube.com (as "Goldwater, Dube Firm"); those links now redirect to 404 pages on goldwaterdroit.com. The firm now uses the name Goldwater Droit and goldwaterdroit.com, and says it has practised family law since 1981. CNAF listed it under Legal Help for separation and divorce involving a child with autism; the site itself does not mention autism. Contact details are from the Contact page.

entries.name: Miriam Foundation
entries.description: Not-for-profit foundation in the Montreal area that funds clinical, educational and leisure programs for people with autism or intellectual disabilities, with or without a diagnosis, at all stages of life, offered at the Gold Centre in Mont-Royal. Services include ABA and Verbal Behavior intervention for children and adults, Early Start Denver Model (ESDM) intervention and parent coaching for young children, creative arts sessions and adult leisure clubs.
entries.cost_note: The Child Programs page says services are partly paid for by families, with the Miriam Foundation subsidizing the balance.
entries.evidence: Clinical intervention services for autism and other neurodevelopmental disorders
entries.notes: fetch.py's text converter drops the main text of miriamfoundation.ca pages (an unclosed <svg> in the Donate button), so the evidence, phone, email and address come from the Clinical Intervention Services brochure (DATA/CMSDOCUMENT/3.pdf, linked from the Child Programs page); the description and cost were read from the saved raw HTML of the About, Gold Centre and Child Programs pages. Families apply through the site's Service Request (intake) page; the Foundation's own line is 514 345-1300.

entries.name: Allocation pour des besoins particuliers – Jeunes (Allowance for Special Needs Program – Youth)
entries.description: Québec government allowance from Aide financière aux études that pays for material resources a child needs at home to keep up with school, such as a computer, adapted peripherals or an augmentative communication device. It is for preschool, elementary and secondary students with a recognized disability causing significant and persistent impairment who attend a recognized unsubsidized private school.
entries.cost_note: Government allowance; the pages do not mention any fee to apply.
entries.evidence: Special needs allowance for youth with a recognized disability resulting in significant and persistent impairment.
entries.notes: CNAF links to two old afe.gouv.qc.ca pages for this program (also under its Funding heading); both now redirect to the general Aide financière aux études page on Québec.ca, and this is the program's current page (French version: quebec.ca/education/aide-financiere-aux-etudes/allocation-besoins-particuliers-jeunes). The child must be assessed before applying, and the devices must be recommended by a health professional. The phone is the Allowance for Special Needs client service line (Québec City area 418-781-0030); page updated July 16, 2026.

entries.name: Allocation pour des besoins particuliers - Adultes (Allowance for special needs - adults)
entries.description: Québec government allowance from Aide financière aux études for students with a disability causing significant and persistent impairment, recognized by a physician, who study in vocational training, adult education, college or university. It pays for disability-related needs for studying that other programs do not cover, such as specialized services, material resources, paratransit and a housing allowance.
entries.cost_note: Government allowance; the pages do not mention any fee to apply.
entries.evidence: This program is a special needs allowance for adults with a recognized disability resulting in significant and persistent impairment.
entries.notes: From CNAF's link to the AFE medical certificate form for major functional disabilities (old afe.gouv.qc.ca URL, now redirected to the general AFE page); that form is used for this allowance and for Loans and Bursaries. Before applying, students must meet the person responsible for students with disabilities at their school, and they can apply online. The phone is the Allowance for Special Needs client service line (Québec City area 418-781-0030).

entries.name: Aide financière aux études (Student Financial Assistance)
entries.description: Québec government student financial aid for full-time and part-time vocational, college and university studies, including the Loans and Bursaries Program, part-time study loans and some scholarships. Students apply online through their Student Financial Assistance file, and the financial aid office at their school can help with applications and forms.
entries.cost_note: Financial aid program; the pages do not mention any fee to apply.
entries.evidence: Get help paying your full-time or part-time studies.
entries.notes: CNAF lists the old mesrs.gouv.qc.ca pages in French and English and the AFE Loans and Bursaries application form (an old afe.gouv.qc.ca URL); all now redirect to the Aide financière aux études page on Québec.ca. The phone is Client Services for the Loans and Bursaries Program (Québec City area 418-643-3750, Montréal area 514-864-3557). Help tied to a disability is in the two Allowance for Special Needs entries.

entries.name: Special Needs Program (St. Patrick's High School, Central Québec School Board)
entries.description: High school of the Central Québec School Board in Québec City. Its support services include a Special Needs Program with special needs technicians and resource teachers, as well as a behaviour technician, psychology and guidance services, a social worker, a nurse and tutoring.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost.
entries.address: 75, rue de Maisonneuve Québec, Québec G1R 2C4
entries.evidence: Special Needs Program including special needs technicians and resource teachers
entries.notes: CNAF links to the school's old page (cqsb.qc.ca/spqc/SpecialNeeds.html), which now returns 403 from a web application firewall; the school's current page on cqsb.qc.ca lists the Special Needs Program under support services. For students enrolled at the school (secondary one to five). The email is the school's general address, not a person's.

entries.name: Association québécoise de musicothérapie (AQM)
entries.description: Quebec association that brings together music therapists, students and others interested in music therapy, and shares information about music therapy and the clinical and ethical standards that govern it. Its public directory, Trouver un musicothérapeute, lets people search for a music therapist by region, client group (including autism spectrum disorder), age group and language.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Promouvoir le développement de services de musicothérapie au Québec
entries.notes: The newest events listed on the site are from 2021, but the member directory still works. Its postal address is a P.O. box in Montréal (C.P. 56053, H3Z 3G3). The mission page loaded only over http (https timed out); the directory page loads over https. The Canadian Association of Music Therapists lists AQM as the Quebec music therapy association.

entries.name: Bartimaeus
entries.description: Canadian company founded in 1988 that provides behavioural support, family support and in-home respite for people of all ages with complex behavioural, emotional or developmental needs, using associates matched to each person by its service coordinators. In Quebec it has service coordinators for the Montreal area and for northern Indigenous communities.
entries.cost_note: The site does not list fees.
entries.evidence: Bartimaeus provides support for family members of all ages, who are exhibiting moderate to severe behavioural difficulties
entries.notes: Head office is in Burlington, Ontario (905 634-2881, admin@bartimaeus.com); the phone here is the Quebec coordinators' line from the Contact page. CNAF also lists Bartimaeus on its New Brunswick page; its Maritimes coordinator works from Truro, Nova Scotia (902 897-9865). The Family Support page says there are no waiting lists for this service.
